gaps.sentence: 'We've been waiting for hours,' the passengers complained. The passengers complained that they ___ waiting for hours.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been waiting → had been waiting after the past reporting verb 'complained'.

gaps.sentence: She ___ me not to worry about the deadline.
gaps.hint: tell sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: Only 'tell' takes a personal object + not to + infinitive; 'said me not to' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: 'I have to catch the last train,' she said. She said she ___ catch the last train.
gaps.explanation: Have to (obligation) backshifts to had to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me his car for the weekend.
gaps.explanation: Offer takes the double-object pattern (offer somebody something); the others do not.

gaps.sentence: 'Who broke the window?' the teacher demanded. The teacher demanded ___ the window.
gaps.explanation: 'Demand to know + wh-clause' with statement order; past simple backshifts to past perfect.
Apologise for + -ing; the other verbs do not take 'for + -ing' in this pattern.

gaps.sentence: 'The shop closes at six,' she reminded me. She reminded me that the shop ___ at six.
gaps.explanation: Even habitual present simple backshifts after a past reporting verb: closes → closed.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't forget to lock up,' my mother said. My mother reminded me ___ up.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't forget' corresponds to remind + object + to-infinitive.
